historical_references.reference: Prashvi was a legendary king of the Vrishni dynasty, mentioned in the Mahabharata. He was the father of Krishna and Vasudeva.
historical_references.context: Mahabharata is an ancient Indian epic that forms a major part of Hindu mythology and Indian literature. It is an approximately 100,000-line Sanskrit epic poem that was probably composed between 400 BCE and 200 BCE.

historical_references.reference: Prashantipura was the capital city of the southern Gangaridai kingdom mentioned in the Puranas and the epic Mahabharata. Prashanti, a son of King Prashasana (who is believed to be a descendant of King Prashvi), was the ruler of Prashantipura.
historical_references.context: Puranas are ancient Hindu texts that contain mythology, philosophy, legends, and historical records. They were composed between 400 BCE and 800 CE.
